description:
STATUS (2026-09-02, HEAD 172ab21f1): LIVE WRONG ANSWER on interp,
refusal on native. Reproducer (session scratchpad sl3.fz):

  defmodule P do
    fn twice(f, x), do: f.(f.(x))
    fn run(f, x), do: twice(f, x)
    fn mk(c), do: fn (n) -> n + c end
  end
  fn main() do
    dbg(P.run(P.mk(1), 10))     # means 12   -- interp prints 12.0
    dbg(P.run(P.mk(0.5), 10))   # means 11.0 -- interp prints 11.0
  end

Both call orders; the int call is always wrong. Native: "closure capture
0 of callable 69 has no single settled representation".

THE MINT IS EXACT (this corrects the two earlier bodies of this ticket).
A closure value's code word names its CONSTRUCTION WRAPPER: one per
producer position, carrying `callable: CallableId` = CallableDescr
(function, arity, capture_tys, capture_shapes, capture_lanes). Native
stamps a fresh identity_fn per wrapper (jobs/native.rs:126, mint :3591;
codegen's callable_boundary_for_identity is 1:1); interp stamps
0x8000_0000|wrapper (ir_interp/backend.rs:1995). In sl3 the two closures
carry DIFFERENT words on both doors. 00411 (same lambda at int/float,
no forwarder, indirect calls through the word) is green on native.

THE LOSS IS ON THE READ SIDE, every reader keyed on ClosureTarget = FnId
(types/closure.rs:18):
 1. Projection: callable_identity_clauses (types/mod.rs:2680-2700) emits
    captures: Vec::new(); callable_identity_targets (:2410) reads only
    lit.fn_id. closure[L](int) and closure[L](float) become ONE
    RuntimeTypePredicate -> one question group -> no discriminating input
    -> run's callsite plan `graph root=n1 -> outcome o0` -> arm 0
    (twice[float]) takes the int closure. This is the wrong answer: the
    int capture lands in a RawF64 lane; the interp's AnyValue::as_float
    accepts Int under the F64 extern marshal, so 10+1.0 = 11.0 then 12.0.
 2. Native identity test: callable_addresses (prim.rs:1370) ORs every
    wrapper with target == fn (surface.rs:85 callable_boundaries_for_
    target, "has to admit all of them").
 3. Interp resolver: backend_callable_identity (ir_interp/backend.rs:
    622-633) maps the wrapper id to wrapper.callable.function, dropping
    wrapper.callable.
 4. Caller-side capture unpack at a grounded direct call: the emitter
    (jobs/native.rs:3850) holds the exact CallableId and coarsens it to
    ClosureTarget(function); lower_closure_capture (prim.rs:1138) then
    demands one repr across ALL wrappers of the fn -> the refusal. The
    interp has no typed unpack (lane count only) and :2784 exempts every
    wrapper word from its function check.
 5. NativeCallableBoundary.target: Option<ClosureTarget> (artifact.rs:
    370) is where the CallableId is dropped (jobs/native.rs:200-203).

PRINCIPLE (review of this ticket, 2026-09-02): a callable value carries
its own annotation, the word. Static knowledge flows by KEY; dynamic
knowledge flows by the WORD. No runtime test re-derives what the mint
stamped; no key specializes on an identity the caller cannot pin.

DESIGN (proposal in session scratchpad kdt127-proposal.md, under cold
review): one notion of callable identity at the runtime grain. The
callable axis element becomes a CallableShape { target, captures:
[RuntimeTypePredicate] } -- per-position recursion exactly as fz-kdt.119's
TupleShapes, AxisPrecision per position; the projection keeps
lit.captures; each construction wrapper carries its projected shape
(materialized with Types); native ORs the addresses of the wrappers whose
shape overlaps the arm's, interp compares shapes (Types-free);
Prim::ClosureCapture carries the physical CallableId. Deletions ride:
the captures erasure, callable_boundaries_for_target + doc,
NativeCallableBoundary.target, dead capture_key, the per-FnId agreement
rule, the interp exemption, the "captures leave no trace" doctrine
(dispatch-matrix.md:65-85 + precision row :270, types/mod.rs:1596,
pipeline.md:29, fz-kdt.125's "one-boundary-per-FnId").

NOT the cure: forwarder key split (splits 3 corpus forwarders, needs a
lit-less closure type, incomplete); consumer collapse (fz-6gb's warned
"stop specializing"; multi-target Absent-carrier call is a refusal today);
capture-read runtime axis (rebuilds the word); generalization at minting
(refuted by prototype in 125); diagnostic backstop (refuses 5 fixtures).

POPULATIONS (census, 466 canon dumps at HEAD): 23 callables minted at
>1 capture layout across 12 fixtures. Same-layout/different-identity
captures (probeB1 static twins 4/9, probeB2 runtime-union 6/-6, 00281,
the six residue groups) are CORRECT today because those lambda bodies
call the captured fn through ITS word (target=-) and are byte-duplicates
-- correctness by not-actually-specializing (waste; own ticket). The
type-differing population (sl3; 00411 without a forwarder) is the wrong
answer.

RELATIONS: fz-kdt.125 (the axis this refines; its record's "one boundary
per FnId" is false), fz-kdt.123 (closes when no-question groups are 0;
this is its remaining half), fz-kdt.157 (its refusal witness becomes
writable), fz-kdt.137 (depth-1 tuple hop; re-test after), fz-6gb
(forwarder erasure unchanged), fz-kdt.152 (layout rule unchanged).

ACCEPTANCE: sl3 prints 12 / 11.0 on interp, JIT, AOT, both orders,
red-first with an Elixir oracle; probeB1/B2/00411/pin6gb unchanged;
callsite_dispatch a_nested_callables_captures_are_not_a_question FLIPS;
residue gate 6 -> 0 or each survivor named (expected: only non-ground-
capture wrappers); 157's red witness written; corpus canon movement
classified (plan movement on the 5 residue fixtures, regained
executables per 123, nothing else); 3-door behaviour sweep 0 movers
except the new fixture; docs rewritten to the surviving truth.

comments.text:
MEASURED by the fz-kdt.125 build (2026-09-01, base bd03d922e). Two premises in
this ticket's body and in fz-kdt.125's spec item 6 are REFUTED:

(1) "13/13 in-corpus groups are identity-separable" is an artifact of the
census helper. Its separability test regexes EVERY closure/fnref name out of a
key, including the ones sitting in CAPTURES -- and a capture is not identity.
Re-measured against the landed axis: the no-question population falls 13 -> 6,
not 13 -> 0. The 6 survivors are THIS ticket's shape exactly, same fn id and
different captures:

  00231_joined_fn_refs_enum_reduce      1  closure[Enum.reduce/3#lambda](fnref[add_a/2])
                                           vs (fnref[add_b/2])
  00277_enum_tier0_fixture              2  same lambda over two different inner closures
  00281_opaque_reducer_closure          1  as 00231
  behavior/opaque_fn_value_join         1  as 00231
  behavior/repr_seam_enum_count_after_reduce2  1  as 00277

(2) "Corpus fallout of the backstop measured ZERO" therefore does not hold. An
unrepresentable-plan DIAGNOSTIC on inseparable groups would refuse to compile
five corpus fixtures. The fz-kdt.125 build did NOT land it for that reason --
the routing half of this ticket is still open and still unbuilt, and it needs
either capture discrimination or a corpus that stops relying on the shape.

WHAT DID LAND, and it is this ticket's ABI half: `Prim::ClosureCapture` reads a
capture back out of a closure through the boundary that WROTE it, and refuses
at compile time when one callable was minted at several capture layouts that
disagree about a slot -- which is samelambda3's shape. That turns "native
executable lowering failed for index 11" into a named invariant failure. The
compile failure itself (interp: "omitted callee value 0 but target 17 needs
semantic inputs") is untouched and still this ticket's.

NOT A LIVE WRONG ANSWER, measured: 00281 with its twin function changed from
`acc + x` to `acc - x` answers -6 on interp and JIT at head. The six groups'
arm-0-takes-all is order-decided but the members are interchangeable on the
probes tried; that is luck, not a proof.

fz-kdt.119 review sequencing (2026-09-01): 119(3)'s recursive identity-preserving erasure ENLARGES this ticket's population ({:tag,#66(int)} vs {:tag,#66(float)} collapse to one question at depth -- same-fn-id/different-capture, one tuple deep). Also this ticket's compile-failure half now has a depth-1 instance with its own ticket (fz-kdt.137) which blocks 119's REFNEST-style acceptance. The backstop-policy decision this ticket owns grows correspondingly.

title: P1: every reader of a closure's runtime identity collapses it to the lambda's FnId while the value's word names its construction -- same lambda at int/float captures: interp prints 12.0 for 12, native refuses
